title.narrative: Kyrgyz Republic Regional Economic Development Project

description.narrative: The Kyrgyz economy grew at an estimated 6.2 percent in 2023, following a 9 percent expansion in 2022. This growth was driven by gold production and a rebound in the agriculture and services sector, particularly services related to transit trade from China and Russia. On the expenditure side, exports and consumption supported growth. Average consumer price inflation declined from 13.8 percent in 2022 to 10.8 percent in 2023 due to easing global food and fuel prices and a tight monetary policy. GDP growth in 2024 is expected to moderate to 4.5 percent as services sector growth decelerates. Investment and exports are expected to drive growth, while consumption growth may ease despite a slight rise in remittances. Without structural reforms, the GDP growth rate is likely to stabilize at 4 percent in the medium term. Inflation is projected to decrease within the target range of 5-7 percent by the end of 2024 and remain stable in the medium term. Despite the Kyrgyz Republic's promising economic performance, poverty remains a significant challenge, impacting approximately 25 percent of the population, particularly in rural areas. The COVID-19 pandemic has further exacerbated existing vulnerabilities, resulting in increased poverty rates and economic hardships for many households. The contrast between rural and urban poverty is stark, particularly in the southern regions, where poverty rates are among the highest in the country. In the Batken and Osh Regions, estimates indicate that over 30 percent of the population lives in poverty. In comparison, Bishkek, the capital, has a relatively lower poverty rate of around 15-20 percent. The RED-1 project serves as a flagship initiative designed to assist the Government in addressing critical regional development challenges. By prioritizing key economic sectors, particularly tourism and agriculture, the Project aims to leverage these industries as primary drivers of local and regional economic growth in the Osh Region. This strategic focus seeks to improve the economic landscape of the region by enhancing key tourism attractions in the cities of Osh and Uzgen and nearby and transforming them into destination hubs for tourism development. Additionally, the Project supports the development of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and startups through customized capacity-building activities aimed at improving business operations and providing financing for high-potential businesses. The Suleiman-Too Complex, a UNESCO-protected site, and Uzgen Archaeological Complex, key investments under the RED-1 Project, hold immense cultural and historical significance for the Kyrgyz Republic. Both sites have faced substantial degradation over the past 30 years, threatening their unique heritage. Revitalizing the Suleiman-Too Complex is particularly crucial for regional development. Osh, where the complex is located, has the potential to become a major tourist destination in the eastern Ferghana Valley. Recognizing the cultural and economic significance of these sites, the Government has sought the Bank's support for their revitalization and included them in the RED-1. However, given the unique skillset required for the preparation of anticipated interventions coincided with limited capacity at both national and local levels, the preparatory phase has taken longer than anticipated, posing risks for its implementation under the Project. To address this issue, the PIU has mobilized extra domestic and international expertise to bridge the capacity gap. In parallel, the Bank has engaged additional consultants to assist stakeholders in meeting UNESCO's stringent requirements and advancing the preparation of design packages. Now that the implementation momentum has been regained, the Government approached the Bank with a request for Additional Financing to address the estimated financing gap of US$8.5 million for the referenced activities and a 23-month time expansion to allow for the completion of flagship investments.
The Project Development Objective is to support the Recipient to enhance regional economic development through targeted interventions in the selected sectors in the Osh region.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries who report effective engagement processes

comment.narrative: The Public Fund “Center for the Development of Rural Municipalities”, under the Small Grants Program in early 2025,, conducted an online survey with 165 program participants, including 57 men (35%) and 108 women (65%). Among the respondents, 160 participants (97%) rated the effectiveness of interaction processes as “Very Good”, comprising 34% men and 66% women. An additional five respondents rated the processes as “Good”, with 60% men and 40% women.

title.narrative: Tourism marketing and promotion activities completed

comment.narrative: Achieved. 7 tourism promotion activities were successfully implemented between 2022 and 2025 to strengthen Osh's positioning as a sustainable tourism destination. These included international forums on geotourism and sustainable tourism, presentations of the Osh Regional Tourism Strategy, participation in the UNESCO General Conference, and a series of regional and international roadshows targeting tour operators in Uzbekistan and the Russian Federation. The efforts culminated in the Second International Tourism Festival “Following the Nomads” in June 2025, further enhancing visibility, stakeholder engagement, and cross-border tourism cooperation.

title.narrative: Tourism marketing and promotion activities completed

comment.narrative: In October 2022, Osh city hosted the UNESCO International Scientific and Practical Forum on Geotourism and the Prospects for Establishing a Geopark in Osh Region, which brought together 54 participants. Attendees included representatives from Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Russia, academics from universities and national academies in Turkey and Kyrgyzstan, national and international geopark experts, as well as officials from tourism and environmental agencies in Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, and other countries. In November 2022, Osh hosted the Second Major Tourism Forum “Developing Sustainable Tourism through Joint Efforts”, featuring the exhibition-fair “Kyrgyzstan on the Great Silk Road”. The forum was attended by representatives of international organizations, tour operators, and districts of Osh Region. title.narrative: People provided with improved urban living conditions

comment.narrative: Achieved. As of February 27, 2026, under Component 3, Subcomponent 3.1, the planned works have been fully completed at selected sites. In Osh city, the interventions included the landscaping of the Osh Drama Theater, improvement of the western section of the Ak Buura River embankment, reconstruction of the central square, renovation of the T. Satylganov Summer Theater, and rehabilitation of A. Navoi Park. In Uzgen city, the works comprised the reconstruction of the city stadium and the adjacent Orto Korgon Park, as well as the construction of a pedestrian bridge. According to ARIS, these interventions have benefited approximately 304,204 people in Osh city and about 20,000 people in Uzgen city, contributing to improved public spaces, enhanced urban functionality, and increased community well being in both cities.

title.narrative: Females participating in the capacity building activities for improved hospitality business practices (gender gap)

comment.narrative: In 2022, training sessions on business planning and procurement procedures were conducted for 161 participants, including 100 women (62%). Additionally, 13 women grant recipients participated in a capacity-building training on improving hospitality practices, organized by the Kyrgyz Resorts Association. In 2023, business planning trainings were held for 311 participants, including 160 women (51%). In 2024, trainings on procurement fundamentals and practical skills, aligned with procurement rules and regulations, were conducted for 175 grant recipients, including 85 women (49%).

title.narrative: Females participating in the capacity building activities for improved hospitality business practices (gender gap)

comment.narrative: On track. Between 2022 and 2025, a series of capacity-building trainings were delivered to Small Grants Program beneficiaries, covering business planning, procurement procedures, and hospitality skills. These trainings reached hundreds of participants annually, with strong female participation across cohorts. Additional specialized sessions on hospitality and marketing were also provided to selected women beneficiaries. In total, 144 women benefited from the program across both grant rounds, including targeted training for tourism-related enterprises, contributing to improved business management and service quality among recipients.

Increase in the sale of agricultural products by project beneficiaries

comment.narrative: On track. The sales growth for beneficiaries who purchased seedlings cannot yet be calculated, as the seedlings are expected to start fruiting only in the third year after planting. For beneficiaries who purchased breeding livestock and equipment, sales have increased by at least 42%, reflecting early positive results from these investments. The reported percentage increase in sales was calculated as a simple arithmetic average of reported sales increases across measured beneficiaries. The mission recommended to ABCC to report in future the weighted average percentage where sales volumes are used as weights. Monitoring is planned for the third quarter of 2026 to determine whether other project beneficiaries have increased their agricultural sales volumes.

title.narrative: Number of operational productive partnership initiatives

comment.narrative: On track. As of February 2026, 26 PPs have been initiated. 12 PPs are fully operational.

So far, 8,280 farmers (including 4,948 women) have been trained in improved agricultural technologies. Each training session presented several improved technologies or good practices in livestock breeding or crop and horticulture production. At the end of the project, there will be a study carried out for the assessment of the project results, including the achievement of the target under this indicator. For now, the ABCC conservatively estimates that at least 50% of the trainees will have adopted at least one improved agricultural technology or good practice learned through the training provided by the project. Thus, the current value of the indicator is 8,280*50%=4,140.

On track. During the project implementation a total of 738 training sessions and consultations were conducted, reaching 13,242 farmers, including 4,450 women. The trainings covered livestock farming, crop and horticultural production, agricultural technologies, marketing, management, and financial literacy. Each training session introduced several improved technologies or good agricultural practices related to livestock breeding and crop or horticultural production. At the end of the project, a dedicated study will be carried out to assess project results, including achievement of the target under this indicator. In the meantime, the ABCC conservatively estimates that at least 50 percent of trained farmers have adopted at least one improved agricultural technology or good practice promoted through the project. Based on this estimate, the current value of the indicator is 13,242 × 50% = 6,621 farmers.
